subject: Chemistry
title: Twins, Round by Round: Lanthanoids vs Actinoids
summary: The two f-block rows below the periodic table (in line, it would be 32 columns wide) look like twins: both fill f orbitals, prefer +3 and contract across the row. But actinoid 5f lies close to 6d and 7s and extends further out, so actinoids reach +3 to +7 (lanthanoids never above +4), contract more, are more reactive, form more complexes and oxo ions such as UO₂²⁺, have more complex magnetism and lower early ionisation enthalpies. Every actinoid is radioactive; among the lanthanoids only promethium is.
keyPoints: **Oxidation states**: Ln mainly +3 (+2, +4), never above +4; An +3 to +7.
**Contraction**: actinoid contraction is greater (5f shields poorly).
**Radioactivity**: only Pm among Ln; all An.
**Bonding**: An more reactive, more complexes, oxo ions such as UO₂²⁺.
**Magnetism** more complex and **early IE** lower for An.

quiz.q: Which series shows oxidation states up to +7?
quiz.explain: Actinoids show +3 to +7, because 5f, 6d and 7s levels are of comparable energies.

quiz.q: The only lanthanoid with no stable isotope is:
quiz.explain: Promethium is the only lanthanoid with no stable isotope (all radioactive; Pm-145 half-life ≈ 17.7 years); all the other lanthanoids have stable isotopes.

quiz.q: Which contraction is greater from element to element?
quiz.explain: Both series contract; the actinoid contraction is greater from element to element because 5f electrons shield poorly.

quiz.q: Which series has the greater tendency to form complexes?
quiz.explain: Actinoids have a greater tendency to form complexes than lanthanoids; their 5f orbitals extend further out and take more part in bonding.

quiz.q: Why are the f-block rows drawn below the table?
options: otherwise the table would be 32 columns wide
quiz.explain: The two rows are drawn separately because inserting them would make the table 32 columns wide.

quiz.q: Which ion exists for an actinoid but has no lanthanoid analogue?
quiz.explain: Early actinoids form linear oxo ions such as UO₂²⁺ (uranyl) and PuO₂²⁺; lanthanoids do not form such ions.

quiz.q: The first ionisation enthalpies of early actinoids compared with early lanthanoids are:
quiz.explain: The first ionisation enthalpies of the early actinoids are lower than those of the early lanthanoids; 5f electrons are farther out and less tightly held.

quiz.q: Magnetic properties are more complex for:
quiz.explain: The magnetic properties of the actinoids are more complex than those of the lanthanoids.

quiz.q: How many f electrons does Am³⁺ have?
quiz.explain: Eu²⁺ has 7 f electrons (4f⁷); Am³⁺ has 6 (5f⁶).
